reviews.text:
Good but not great yet…. The most useful feature is being able to dictate what you’ve eaten in plain language or scan an item’s barcode. However, the biggest downside is the lack of real-time calorie tracking with Apple Health integration. For example, if my daily limit is 1,800 calories but I log 2,400, I want the app to show I’m 600 over. But if I’ve also burned 1,000 calories exercising, I’d like it to reflect that I’m actually 400 under my allowance.

I’d also love the option to create and save specific meals and reuse them without having to re-enter every ingredient or search through previous days for that meal. For instance, if I often make a two-egg, three-mushroom, tablespoon of olive oil, and one-cup spinach omelette, it would be great to select that saved “meal” instead of typing it in each time or looking back to see when I last made it. The same goes for other recurring meals, like a fruit and protein shake with half a banana, a cup of blueberries, three slices of mango, and a quarter cup of protein powder.

Basic Tracking Only. It’s important to remember this app just keeps a running daily log of your food calorie, fat, carb intake. It is great if that’s your goal. However, if you are tracking macros and micros for health issues, this app is probably not for you. For example, this app will give you an estimated breakdown of macros for a meal by photo, but scanning a particular brand item, like a marinade, won’t bring up useful or accurate info. So things like sodium may not be tracked accurately. Also, your meals aren’t separated, they just accumulate. There are a slew of better tracking apps if those values are of concern to you. But, for keeping track of an estimated daily calorie or carb intake, this app may work.
